title: Inglés B1 · Evaluación diagnóstica · Forma A · Diagnóstico de entrada

parts.title: Part A — Short messages
parts.instructions: Listen and choose the correct answer.

items.prompt: What time does the heritage tour start?

audio.transcript: Good afternoon. Could you tell me what time the heritage walking tour starts tomorrow? — Of course. It begins at nine fifteen from the main square.

items.prompt: How much is the reef tour per person?

audio.transcript: The guided reef tour costs one hundred and twenty thousand pesos per person, life jacket included.

items.prompt: Where is breakfast served?

competence.raw: M-II · 2.1 · voz pasiva en presente (servicios) · listening

audio.transcript: Breakfast is served on the terrace from seven, and the rooms are cleaned every morning.

items.prompt: Where is the gala dinner going to be held?

audio.transcript: Next Friday the gala dinner is going to be held at the old customs house, not at the beach club.

items.prompt: What must visitors do on the boat?

audio.transcript: All visitors must wear a life jacket on the boat; you ought to protect the reef by staying on the marked route.

parts.title: Part B — Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to each conversation and choose the correct answer.

items.prompt: How does the host respond to the complaint?

audio.transcript: — I’m really disappointed; the noise from the building work is frustrating. — I completely understand, and I’m sorry. I see your point; however, the work stops at six.

items.prompt: Why is the host apologizing?

competence.raw: M-I · 1.4 · presente perfecto + disculpa profesional · listening

options.text: because they have moved the event

audio.transcript: — I’m sorry, we have moved the gala dinner to the plaza because of a new local regulation. It’s going to start at eight instead.

items.prompt: What does the gallery offer the customer?

competence.raw: M-III · 3.1 · devoluciones/situaciones inusuales + modales para ofrecer · listening

options.text: an exchange or a store credit

audio.transcript: — This sculpture arrived damaged. Could I get a refund? — I’m very sorry. According to our policy we can offer you an exchange or a store credit.

items.prompt: What does Elena recommend?

options.text: the night market and the concert

audio.transcript: — We have one free evening in town. — I recommend visiting the night market, and you should book the candlelight concert.

items.prompt: How does the tourist feel?

competence.raw: M-III · 3.3 · sentimientos tras un faux pas + 2.º condicional ligero · listening
competence.topic: sentimientos tras un faux pas + 2.º condicional ligero

audio.transcript: — A tourist photographed the ceremony without permission. — He feels embarrassed and regrets it. If you asked the leaders first, you wouldn’t offend anyone.

parts.title: Part B — A heritage tour note
parts.instructions: Read the text and answer the questions.

shared.title: Heritage tour note
shared.text: Welcome to the old town! While the guide was explaining the legend of the lighthouse, which has warned sailors for two hundred years, a sudden storm began, so we moved indoors. The colonial houses are protected by the community, and the coral reef is now managed by local families. Tomorrow the sunrise boat trip is going to leave at six, although it will be a little shorter than usual because the sea is rough.

items.prompt: What was the guide doing when the storm began?

competence.raw: M-II · 2.4 · pasado simple vs. continuo · reading

options.text: explaining the legend of the lighthouse

items.prompt: How is the lighthouse described in the text?

options.text: as the lighthouse which has warned sailors for two hundred years

items.prompt: Who manages the coral reef now?

competence.raw: M-II · 2.1 · voz pasiva en presente · reading

items.prompt: When is the sunrise boat trip going to leave?

items.prompt: Professional apology email (70-100 words). Write a professional apology email to Sarah: the ocean tour has been canceled and the gala dinner has been moved. Explain what has happened (present perfect), what is going to happen now (future forms) and offer a concrete alternative. Close politely.
items.source_rubric: formal register · present perfect for what happened · future forms for the new plan · clear alternative + polite apology · cohesion and spelling

items.prompt: Balanced report + storytelling (70-100 words). Write a balanced report of the day on the coast: what went wrong and how the community solved it. Use past simple and past continuous, connectors (although/however/but) and briefly narrate the positive outcome (resilience / culture of peace). Include at least one comparison (-er than / more ... than).
items.source_rubric: balanced contrast (negative to positive) · past simple and continuous · narrative connectors · narration of resilience · one comparison · intelligibility

parts.title: Speaking (written answer)
parts.instructions: Write your answer in English, as if you were speaking.

items.prompt: Clarify, compare and recommend (mini-pitch). At reception: handle a complaint, ask for clarification with an indirect question (Could you tell me...?), compare two plan options (as...as / -er than) and finish with a personalised recommendation using a relative clause (the tour which... / a guide who...).

questions.text: Write what you would say here.

items.source_rubric: clarifies with an indirect question · compares two options · recommends with a relative clause · intelligibility

source_notes: b1-fa-l-11: source item 11 is the matching task; it counts as 5 items and is left out of the per-module map

b1-fa-w-01 and b1-fa-w-02: the source asks for 70-100 words. The platform keeps 900 characters of each answer (the shared cap of 300 would cut an email at about 45 words) and serves 70 and 100 as a hint; the rubric counts words in a wider window

Speaking Task 1 (b1-fa-s-01, read the Writing email aloud) is NOT in this form: it has no written equivalent yet and needs a pedagogical decision. The Speaking section keeps its 15% weight and holds Task 2 only (0 to 5)
Speaking is delivered as a typed answer (delivery: written_equivalent); it does not measure pronunciation

The source has no figure briefs or alt text, so no item has an image and image_pending is not set anywhere; it also gives no instructions per part, so the part titles and instructions are ours (see REVIEW-B1-checkin.md)
